timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. - "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

They're the same app. Cloud Run gives every service two web addresses, and both point to the same running version, so there's nothing different behind them.

- **https://pawse-114215092948.europe-west6.run.app** is the newer, predictable format: service name, project number, region. You can work it out without deploying, and it stays the same if the service is recreated. **Use this one.**
- **https://pawse-ewt2scevfq-oa.a.run.app** is the older format: a random hash plus a short region code (`oa` = europe-west6). Google still issues it for compatibility.

The deploy script allows both addresses, so either one works.

The script's final `Live:` line prints the old hash-style address because that's what Cloud Run reports as the service's main URL. I can change it to print the project-number one so it matches the README, if you'd like.

content.content:
---
name: demo-check
description: >-
  Verify the Pawse demo story end to end in a real browser and through the API, capture screenshots,
  and check console errors. Use when someone says "does the demo work", "check the demo",
  "take screenshots", or before feature freeze and before pitching.
---

# Demo check

The demo story in [research/pet-insurance/demo-video-script.md](../../../research/pet-insurance/demo-video-script.md)
is the acceptance test.

## 1. Automated first

```bash
bash scripts/check.sh                                   # safety, skills, JS syntax, OpenAPI, pytest
uvicorn pawse.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765      # in a second terminal
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/docs >/dev/null && echo up
```

The rehearsal and demo-policy search work without provider keys. Story logic belongs in pytest
(`tests/test_orchestration.py`): assert visible outcomes (costs, citations, statuses), not internals.

## 2. Browser walkthrough

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 and click through every scene of the story. With browser automation
(Playwright or the Chrome extension), capture a screenshot per scene and collect console errors:

```js
page.on("console", (m) => m.type() === "error" && errors.push(m.text()));
```

Look at every screenshot: overflow, cut-off text, mobile/narrow width, loading and error states,
"simulated" labels visible on every fake step. Keep screenshots out of git unless they go in the README.

## 3. Real providers

With keys in `.env`: run the care flow once with real Gemini, a voice preview with Gradium (owner
consent), and `python scripts/probe_models.py` for model access. Record results in
[docs/VALIDATION.md](../../../docs/VALIDATION.md); do not claim anything that did not run.

## 4. Demo-day checklist

- [ ] Story passes 3 times in a row on the demo machine (LLMs are flaky: tighten prompts or fake the step)
- [ ] Works on venue Wi-Fi / phone hotspot; rehearsal mode as last resort
- [ ] Microphone permission granted in the demo browser; backup video exists ([pitch](../pitch/SKILL.md))
- [ ] Zoom, notifications off, tabs pre-opened, demo state reset

## Keep this skill current

Keep commands in sync with the README quick start. Run `python scripts/validate_skills.py` after editing.
# Browser and real-speech tests (issue #25)

Automated versions of the manual checks in [docs/VALIDATION.md](../../docs/VALIDATION.md): microphone capture,
audio upload, desktop layout, the Gemini Live voice client, and recognition of English, Chinese, German and Hindi
speech. They drive the shipped pages: the React app at `/app` (built from `web/`) and the original page at `/`.

## Run

```bash
pip install -r requirements-e2e.txt && python -m playwright install chromium
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e                      # 62 browser tests, no keys, about 75 s
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e -k live_voice --headed   # watch one file
```

The suite (re)builds `web/dist` whenever it is missing or older than a `web/` source (needs Node), so it always
tests your current frontend. `bash scripts/check.sh` skips the browser tests and runs only the speech-metric tests.
Layout screenshots land in `test-results/layout/` (git-ignored) for a human look.

## What runs, and how without hardware or keys

| File | Page | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |

content.text:
Everything works on the deployed version, with no console errors on any page I tested. I found four things worth fixing, mainly how the results are labelled and displayed.

**What I tested** (https://pawse-114215092948.europe-west6.run.app):

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| API: health, capabilities, Mimi rehearsal, policy, policy search, voice status | ✅ all 200 |
| Real Gemini: care request, agent run, German vet script, live token | ✅ guidance comes back as "contact vet" in 4 to 7 s; real Zurich clinics with phone numbers from Gemini + Google Maps; German script is clean |
| AI consent off | ✅ falls back to safe generic guidance and flags `ai_consent_required` |
| `/` Mimi story, all 6 scenes with the choices clicked | ✅ every scene is labelled "Simulated"; CHF 385 vs 510 and the policy references are correct |
| `/` live care form and German script, in the browser | ✅ |
| `/app/` scripted demo | ✅ call Pawse → limping → jumped → 🟡 see a vet today → pick clinic → simulated German vet call → 16:30 → summary |
| `/app/?live=1` Gemini Live | ✅ consent screen → token → Live socket → Pawse greets. A typed message triggered the backend tool, then "Contact a vet today" and a list of real clinics. "Prepare vet conversation" opens the draft screen with "No call placed" and a dial button. |
| Phone width (390 px) | ✅ no sideways scrolling on either page |

**Issues:**
- ⚠️ **Rule 3 (honesty):** at the end of the `/app/` scripted demo, the plan card says **"✓ Booked 16:30 · ≈ CHF 600"** with no "simulated" label. The call screen itself is labelled correctly.
- ⚠️ **Live clinic list in `/app/`:** the header says "Sorted by distance", but every distance shows "–" because Gemini Maps returns no coordinates. Each card also shows a raw timestamp like `2026-10-10T14:46:16.141784+00:00`, and says "Hours unknown" even when opening hours are listed. On `/`, the first clinic was in Kilchberg rather than one near the city centre.
- ⚠️ **Live advice card in `/app/`:** the "Right now" section lists questions for the vet and services to ask about, not what to do right now. The scripted demo shows the right kind of advice there.
- ⚠️ **Location with AI consent off:** if the owner gives location consent but turns AI consent off, the coordinates still go to Gemini for the clinic search. The code does this on purpose and sends only coordinates, but the location consent text may need to say that Google gets them.

**Not tested:** cloning the owner's own voice and Gradium audio (needs a real recording and spends credits), speech recognition with a real voice (the test browser's microphone only plays a test sound), photo upload, and the insurer call in the `/app/` scripted demo.

Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-azureuser-pawse/abbd5329-e9b7-4793-9b17-11b65fb12ad2/scratchpad/shots/`.

Should I fix the four issues? I'd start with the "Booked" label and the clinic list.

async def google_clinics(req, client):
    key = os.getenv("GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        raise ProviderError("google_places_not_configured")
    fields = "places.id,places.displayName,places.formattedAddress,places.location,places.internationalPhoneNumber,places.googleMapsUri,places.websiteUri,places.rating,places.currentOpeningHours"
    r = await client.post("https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchNearby", headers={"X-Goog-Api-Key": key, "X-Goog-FieldMask": fields}, json={
        "includedTypes": ["veterinary_care"], "maxResultCount": 20, "rankPreference": "DISTANCE",
        "locationRestriction": {"circle": {"center": {"latitude": req.location.lat, "longitude": req.location.lng}, "radius": req.radius_km * 1000}},
    }, timeout=15)
    r.raise_for_status()
    result = []
    for p in r.json().get("places", []):
        location = Location(lat=p["location"]["latitude"], lng=p["location"]["longitude"])
        phone = p.get("internationalPhoneNumber")
        opening = p.get("currentOpeningHours", {}).get("openNow")
        result.append(Clinic(id=p["id"], name=p["displayName"]["text"], address=p.get("formattedAddress", ""),
                             phone=phone, call_url=phone_uri(phone), location=location,
                             distance_km=distance(req.location, location), rating=p.get("rating"),
                             maps_url=safe_url(p.get("googleMapsUri")), website=safe_url(p.get("websiteUri")),
                             open_now=opening if isinstance(opening, bool) else None,
                             source="google_places", retrieved_at=now()))
    return result


def normalize_mapify(summary, detail, origin):
    place = detail.get("detail", {}).get("place", {})
    # The upstream generic health category is insufficient to assert veterinary care.
    text = " ".join(str(x) for x in [place.get("name", summary.get("name", "")), place.get("category", ""), summary.get("category", ""), *place.get("detailed_characteristics", [])]).lower()
    if not any(word in text for word in ("veterinar", "veterinär", "tierarzt", "tierklinik", "animal hospital", "pet hospital")):
        return None
    loc = place.get("location") or summary.get("location")
    try:
        loc = Location.model_validate(loc) if loc else None
    except ValueError:
        loc = None
    phone = place.get("phone")
    name = place.get("name") or summary.get("name") or "Veterinary clinic"
    # Upstream code defaults missing opening hours to open: never propagate that assumption.
    return Clinic(id=str(summary.get("place_id") or summary.get("id")), name=name,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start branch work in a new linked worktree, never in the shared root checkout.
#
#   bash scripts/worktree.sh <type>/<slug>      e.g. bash scripts/worktree.sh fix/clinic-hours
#
# type: feat | fix | chore | docs | test | research (AGENTS.md rule 7)
# Creates <parent-of-root>/pawse-wt/<slug> on a new branch <type>/<slug> off a freshly
# fetched origin/main, copies .env if the root checkout has one, and prints next steps.
# Works from the root checkout or from inside any worktree. PAWSE_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR
# overrides the base directory (tests use it).
set -euo pipefail

die() { printf 'worktree.sh: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

branch="${1:-}"
[ -n "$branch" ] || die "usage: bash scripts/worktree.sh <feat|fix|chore|docs|test|research>/<slug>"
case "$branch" in
  feat/* | fix/* | chore/* | docs/* | test/* | research/*) ;;
  *) die "branch '$branch' must start with feat/, fix/, chore/, docs/, test/ or research/" ;;
esac
slug="${branch#*/}"
printf '%s' "$slug" | grep -Eq '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$' \
  || die "slug '$slug' must be lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' (no slashes)"
case "$slug" in *..*) die "slug '$slug' must not contain '..'" ;; esac

# The root checkout, asked of git: from inside a worktree the common dir is still root's .git.
common_dir="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" \
  || die "run this inside the pawse repo"
root="$(dirname "$common_dir")"
base="${PAWSE_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR:-$(dirname "$root")/$(basename "$root")-wt}"
dir="$base/$slug"

[ -e "$dir" ] && die "$dir already exists. Reuse it (cd $dir) or pick another slug."

git -C "$root" fetch --quiet origin || die "git fetch origin failed"
if git -C "$root" ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  die "branch $branch already exists on origin. Pick another slug, or attach to it: git -C $root worktree add $dir $branch"
fi
git -C "$root" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$branch" \
  && die "local branch $branch already exists. Attach to it: git -C $root worktree add $dir $branch"

new_head = '''#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy the public demo to Cloud Run: bash scripts/deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project> [region]
# One instance (min=max=1): the case cache in pawse/state.py is in memory.
# Provider keys come from .env (PAWSE_ENV_FILE overrides; a worktree without .env uses the root checkout's):
# each one set there is synced to its Secret Manager secret (a new version only when the value changed) and
# mounted. A key missing from .env keeps the secret already deployed. Values are never printed.
set -euo pipefail
PROJECT="${1:?usage: deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project> [region]}"
REGION="${2:-europe-west6}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
# ENV_VAR=secret-name for every key the app reads. Add new provider keys here.
KEYS="GEMINI_API_KEY=pawse-gemini-key REDACTED GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=pawse-places-key"
ENV_FILE="${PAWSE_ENV_FILE:-.env}"
[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || ENV_FILE="$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")/.env"
env_value() {  # last NAME=value line, surrounding quotes removed
  [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || return 0
  sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*\\(export[[:space:]]\\+\\)\\?$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p" "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n 1 | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e "s/^[\\"']\\(.*\\)[\\"']$/\\1/"
}
RUNTIME_SA="$(gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" --format 'value(projectNumber)')-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com"
SECRETS=""
for pair in $KEYS; do
  var="${pair%%=*}" secret="${pair#*=}" value="$(env_value "${pair%%=*}")"
  if [ -n "$value" ]; then
    if ! gcloud secrets describe "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf %s "$value" | gcloud secrets create "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" --replication-policy automatic --data-file=- --quiet
      echo "$var: created secret $secret"
    elif [ "$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret "$secret" --project "$PROJECT")" != "$value" ]; then
      printf %s "$value" | gcloud secrets versions add "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" --data-file=- --quiet
      echo "$var: new version of $secret"
    else
      echo "$var: $secret is up to date"
    fi
    gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" --member "serviceAccount:$RUNTIME_SA" \\
      --role roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor --quiet >/dev/null
  elif gcloud secrets describe "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$var: not in $ENV_FILE, keeping the deployed secret $secret"
  else
    echo "$var: not set, skipped"
    continue
  fi
  SECRETS="${SECRETS:+$SECRETS,}$var=$secret:latest"
done
case ",$SECRETS" in *,GEMINI_API_KEY=*) ;; *) echo "GEMINI_API_KEY is required: set it in $ENV_FILE" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
'''
s = new_head + s[len(old_head):]

EOF

### Public demo (Cloud Run)

The `Dockerfile` builds the React app in `web/` and runs it with the API as one container. `scripts/deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project>` deploys it to Cloud Run with one instance (the case cache is in memory), keys from Secret Manager (`pawse-gemini-key`, optional `pawse-gradium-key`) and these public-demo settings:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
docs/VALIDATION.md:7:- Clinic discovery and owner insurance profile (2026-10-10): 106 backend tests plus web checks pass. The project's Gemini key is blocked for Places API (HTTP 403), but Gemini Grounding with Google Maps (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) works with it. One real `POST /api/v1/care/requests` at Zurich's public centre (10 km, `share_with_ai: false`) returned HTTP 201 in 3.2 s with 32 clinics: 9 Google Maps listings (all with phone, address and Maps link; parsed from grounding sources, not model text) and 23 from the local OSM snapshot; 11 snapshot rows lack a phone. Google Maps listings carry no coordinates, so their distance is unknown and two listings likely beyond 10 km could not be filtered. Results vary between calls. Browser check: the static care form rendered the cards with call, map, website and Google Maps attribution; the React home screen saved an owner insurer and plan on the device. Gemini Live asking for the insurer was covered by mocked tool tests only, not a spoken session.
docs/VALIDATION.md:36:- Live clinic discovery: no Mapify backend URL or Google Places key was supplied. Only provider adapters and normalization are tested.
docs/VALIDATION.md:83:- Not verified on the public URL: clinic search (no Places key or Mapify configured, so care results are `partial`), Gradium voice cloning, Gemini Live voice.

It returns up to 20 nearby places, including phone and current opening state when available. It requires Maps Platform API enablement, restrictions and billing; a Gemini key alone is not proof of Places access. There is no silent fallback between paid providers.

content.text:
Distances now work on the live site. A clinic request near Zurich HB returns 20 real vet practices, each with a straight-line distance and open/closed status, and the deploy now carries the keys over from `.env`.

**🛑 The key alone made clinic search worse.** When I tested it locally, the Places search the app was using (Nearby Search by `veterinary_care` type) returned a pharmacy, a psychologist, a bird charity, homeopaths and an entry called "PlaceHolder". Places takes priority over Gemini Maps, so deploying the key as things stood would have made the clinic list worse. I switched to Places Text Search for "Tierarztpraxis Kleintierpraxis Tierklinik" with strict vet-type filtering, and drop anything outside the search radius. I wrote the test first and saw it fail before the fix. The full check suite passes.

**Keys on deploy:** `scripts/deploy_cloudrun.sh` now reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GRADIUM_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` from `.env` and:
- creates the matching secret if it doesn't exist, or adds a new version only when the value changed;
- gives the Cloud Run service account access and attaches every key to the service;
- keeps the already-deployed secret if a key is missing from `.env`, and never prints values.

On this run it created `pawse-places-key`, and the Gemini and Gradium secrets already matched `.env`. A new provider key needs one entry in the script's `KEYS` list.

**Live result** (https://pawse-114215092948.europe-west6.run.app): clinic sources are now `google_places` then `gemini_maps`. The first results were Tierspital (2.75 km), VET Zentrum Letzigrund (2.82 km) and Kleintierklinik Oberstrass (0.9 km). `/` and `/app/` both return 200.

PR (merged): https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/pull/64

Remaining issues:
- ⚠️ Places lists "Pferdekliniken", a horse clinic at the Tierspital, among the cat results.
- ⚠️ Clinics that report being open are listed first, so the nearest one (Oberstrass, 0.9 km, closed now) comes 5th. The `/app/` header still says "Sorted by distance", which doesn't match.
- The four issues from the earlier test are still open, including the "✓ Booked 16:30" card in the scripted demo with no "simulated" label.

    key = os.getenv("GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY")

        raise ProviderError("google_places_not_configured")
    fields = "places.id,places.displayName,places.formattedAddress,places.location,places.internationalPhoneNumber,places.googleMapsUri,places.websiteUri,places.rating,places.currentOpeningHours,places.businessStatus,places.regularOpeningHours.weekdayDescriptions,places.userRatingCount"
    # Nearby Search by type alone also returns places Google merely tags as veterinary (homeopaths, associations,

    r = await client.post("https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchText", headers={"X-Goog-Api-Key": key, "X-Goog-FieldMask": fields}, json={

    r.raise_for_status()
